SCOPE AND FIELD OF APPLICATION

5.4 5.5

Sucrose (C12H220,,

1.

This International Standard specifies a reference method for the determination of the protein content of caseins and caseinates, excluding those containing ammonium caseinate or other ammonium compounds, or other nitrogenous nonprotein compounds.

Boric acid, 40 g/l solution. hydroxide, concentrated aqueous solution,

5.6 Sodium 30 % (m/m).

2

REFERENCES

ISO/R 707, Milk and milk products - Sampling. IS0 331 O/I, Test sieves - Technical requirements and testing - Part I : Metal wire cloth. IS0 5550, Caseins and caseinates - Determination of water content (Reference method). l)

0,l N standard 5.7 Hydrochloric acid, approximately volumetric solution, standardized against sodium tetraborate decahydrate (Na,B,O,. lOH,O) or anhydrous sodium carbonate (NazCOa). 5.8 Mixed indicator

Mix equal volumes of a 2 g/l solution of methyl red in at least 95 % (V/l/) ethanol and a 1 g/i solution of methylene blue in at least 95 % (V/V) ethanol.

3

DEFINITION 6 6.1 6.2 APPARATUS Analytical balance Kjeldahl flask, 500 ml capacity.

protein content of caseins and caseinates : The nitrogen content as determined by the procedure described in this International Standard, multiplied by 6,38 and expressed as a percentage by mass.

4

PRINCIPLE

Digestion of a test portion with a mixture of potassium sulphate and sulphuric acid, in the presence of copper sulphate as catalyst, to convert organic nitrogen into ammoniacal nitrogen. Distillation and absorption of the ammonia in boric acid solution. Titration with standard volumetric hydrochloric acid solution. Multiplication of the result by the factor 6,38.

6.3 Digestion apparatus to hold the Kjeldahl flask (6.2) in an inclined position and with a heating device which will not heat the part of the flask above the surface of the liquid contents. 6.4 Condenwr with straight inner tube.

5

REAGENTS

6.5 Outlet tube with safety bulb connected to the lower end of the condenser (6.4) by a ground glass joint or a rubber tube. If rubber tubing is used, the glass ends must be near one another. 6.6 Splash-head connected to the Kjeldahl flask (6.2) and to the condenser (6.4) by soft, close-fitting rubber stoppers. 6.7 6.8 6.9 Conical flask, 500 ml capacity. Graduated cylinders, 50 ml and 100 ml capacity. Burette, 50 ml capacity, graduated in 0,l ml.

All reagents shall be of recognized analytical quality. The water used shall be distilled water or water of at least equivalent purity. 5.1 5.2 5.3 Sulphuric acid, concentrated, pzo 1,84 g/ml. Potassium sulphate. anhydrous ( K,S04). Copper sulphate pantahydrate (CuS04.5Hz0).
